THIS APPEAL COMING ON FOR ORDERS, THROUGH PHYSICAL HEARING/VIDEO CONFERENCING THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT

Aggrieved by the judgment and award dated 13.12.2019 passed in MVC No.2008/2019 by the V Additional Small Causes Judge & XXIV ACMM, Member, MACT, Bengaluru (for short 'the Tribunal'), the petitioners therein have preferred this appeal.

sentences.text:
Petitioner No.1 is the wife and petitioners Nos.2 to 5 are the children of the deceased and they have preferred MVC No.2008/2019.
4.

The Tribunal, based on the evidence let in, has awarded a compensation of Rs.12,40,000/- along with interest @ 9% p.a. under the following heads:-
1 Loss of dependency Rs. 11,70,000/- 2 Loss of consortium Rs. 40,000/-

3 Loss of estate Rs. 15,000/-
Towards funeral and 4 Rs. 15,000/-
obsequies ceremonies Total Rs. 12,40,000/-
5. Not satisfied by the same, the petitioners have preferred this appeal.
6. Admittedly, the accident happened in the year 2019.
The petitioners have not established income of the deceased before the Tribunal.
Hence, the income of the deceased is notionally fixed at Rs.14,000/- per month.
The age of the deceased at the time of the accident was 49 years.
Given the age of the deceased, as per the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Sarla Verma & Ors vs Delhi Transport Corp.& Anr [2009(6) SCC 121], multiplier of '13' is applicable.

As per the law laid down by the Apex Court in National Insurance Co.Ltd. v. Pranay Sethi (2017) 16 SCC 680, 25%
needs to be added to his income.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Further, the deceased who had five dependants at the time of his death, 3/4th of his income has to be deducted towards his personal expenses.

Thus, on the count of 'loss of dependency', the petitioners would be entitled to a sum of Rs.20,47,500/-
(14000+25%x13x12x3/4=20,47,500).

Further, each of the petitioners are entitled to a sum of Rs.40,000/- and together they are entitled to a sum of Rs.2,00,000/- (40,000x5=2,00,000)
towards 'loss of consortium'.

Further, they are entitled to a sum of Rs.30,000/- towards 'funeral expenses' and 'loss of estate'.
7.

sentences.text: Thus, the petitioners are entitled to a sum of Rs.22,77,500/-.
However, Tribunal has come to the conclusion that the deceased himself is responsible for the accident to an extent of 10% and the said fact is not disputed by the petitioners.
Hence, after deducting 10% , the Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.11,16,000/-.

Thus, the petitioners would be entitled to a total compensation of Rs.20,49,750/-
i.e., after deducting 10% from Rs.22,77,500/-.
Therefore, the petitioners are entitled to an enhanced compensation of Rs.9,33,750/- (Rs.20,49,750/- minus Rs.11,16,000/- = Rs.9,33,750/-).

Hence, the following:
ORDER i. Appeal is allowed in part.
ii.

The total compensation awarded by the Tribunal is modified and petitioners are entitled to enhanced compensation of Rs.9,33,750/- (Rupees Nine Lakhs Thirty Three Thousand Seven Hundred and Fifty only) over and above what has been already awarded by the Tribunal along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of filing of the petition before the Tribunal till the date of realization.

iii. Respondent No.1 shall pay the enhanced compensation amount to the petitioners along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. within a period of six weeks from the date of receipt of the certified copy of the judgment and order.
iv. Draw modified award accordingly.
